title: Southern Magnolia: Ancient Magnolias You Can Visit
meta_description: Flowers the width of a dinner plate, lemon scented, gone in two days. Thirteen old southern magnolias mapped, the oldest on a Rome pavement.
intro: For a few weeks in early summer this tree opens cream white flowers the width of a dinner plate, lemon scented and finished within a couple of days. Magnolia grandiflora comes from the warm swamp forests of the American southeast and only reached Europe in the middle of the eighteenth century, which puts a hard ceiling on how old any of these can be. The oldest here is Rome's, roughly 275 years, and it does not stand in a garden at all: it grows on the pavement of Via Corsini, outside the wall of the palace whose garden it was planted for. Padua's went in during 1786, the year Goethe came through the gate. Frederick Douglass planted two at Cedar Hill for his wife, on family testimony rather than a receipt. Thirteen mapped, in ten cities, and the leaves stay glossy and green all winter.
